chats.answer:
Yes! A NAS (Network Attached Storage) can absolutely host a Minecraft server for you and your friends, 24/7. In fact, a good NAS can run Minecraft alongside file storage, backups, Plex, and other services.

However, not all NAS devices are good Minecraft servers. The most important thing is CPU performance, not storage capacity.

What makes a good Minecraft NAS?

Component

	

Recommended




CPU

	

Intel Core i3/i5 or better, preferably modern




RAM

	

16 GB minimum for a NAS doing multiple jobs




Storage

	

SSD or NVMe for Minecraft world files




Software

	

Docker support or virtual machines




Network

	

Gigabit Ethernet or better




OS

	

Linux-based NAS OS with container support

For a typical Minecraft Java server with 5–10 friends, I'd allocate around 4–6 GB RAM to Minecraft, more for modpacks.

Minecraft Java Edition relies heavily on single-core CPU performance. A NAS with a modern Intel processor can outperform a much more expensive NAS with an older, slower server CPU.

How your friends connect

You install Minecraft in a Docker container, keep the NAS running, and let friends join using your public IP address or a domain name.

You can forward TCP port 25565 on your router or use a Minecraft tunnel service if port forwarding isn't available. Keep the NAS administration interface private, enable the Minecraft whitelist, and back up your world.

One important alternative

If you only want to host Minecraft, rather than also needing a NAS for storage, a mini PC with a modern Intel Core i5 or AMD Ryzen processor and 16 GB RAM will often give you better game performance per dollar.
